unesco_raw.name_en: Historic Centre of Rome, the Properties of the Holy See
unesco_raw.short_description_en: Founded according to legend in 753 BC, Rome was first the centre of the Roman Republic, then of the Roman Empire, and became the capital of the Christian world in the 4th century.
Built on the site of an Etruscan settlement, Florence, the symbol of the Renaissance, rose to economic and cultural pre-eminence under the Medici in the 15th and 16th centuries.

unesco_raw.name_en: Archaeological Areas of Pompei, Herculaneum and Torre Annunziata
unesco_raw.short_description_en: Buried by the eruption of Vesuvius in AD 79, the Roman towns of Pompeii and Herculaneum provide a complete and vivid picture of society and daily life at a specific moment in the past.
Founded in the 5th century and spread over 118 small islands, Venice became a major maritime power in the 10th century and is an extraordinary architectural masterpiece.
Built continuously from the 3rd century BC to the 17th century AD on the northern border of the country as the great military defensive project of successive Chinese Empires.

unesco_raw.name_en: Imperial Palaces of the Ming and Qing Dynasties in Beijing and Shenyang
unesco_raw.short_description_en: Seat of supreme power for over five centuries, the Forbidden City with its landscaped gardens and nearly 10,000 rooms is a priceless testimony to Chinese civilization.

unesco_raw.name_en: Mausoleum of the First Qin Emperor
unesco_raw.short_description_en: Guarded by the famous Terracotta Warriors, the tomb of Qin Shi Huang in Shaanxi showcases the military, artistic and technological achievements of unified imperial China.
Begun in 1248 and completed in 1880, this Gothic masterpiece houses the shrine of the Three Kings and testifies to the enduring strength of European Christian architecture.
A 65 km stretch of the Rhine where dramatic river terraces, vineyards, historic towns and forty hilltop castles trace two millennia of European transport and Romantic culture.
Perched on a rocky islet in the midst of vast sandbanks exposed to powerful tides between Normandy and Brittany stands the Gothic Benedictine abbey dedicated to the Archangel Michael.
Embellished by generations of architects, sculptors and landscape designers under Louis XIV, Versailles served as the ideal model of a royal residence across Europe for over a century.
Rising above Granada at the foot of the Sierra Nevada, the Alhambra and the Generalife gardens preserve the finest surviving palaces and courtyards of Nasrid Islamic Spain.
An immense mausoleum of white marble built in Agra between 1631 and 1648 by order of the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his favourite wife, the jewel of Muslim art in India.
One of the greatest Maya centres of the Yucatán peninsula, illustrating the fusion of Maya and Toltec architectural visions in monuments such as El Castillo and the Great Ball Court.
The most ARCHITECTURALLY sophisticated prehistoric stone circles in the world, demonstrating Neolithic and Bronze Age ceremonial design and astronomical alignment.
Imperial capital of Japan from its foundation in 794 until the mid-19th century, Kyoto shaped the development of Japanese wooden religious architecture and the art of the garden.
The finest surviving example of early 17th-century Japanese castle architecture, comprising 83 wooden buildings with elegant white plastered earthen walls.
Founded by Darius I in 518 BC as the ceremonial capital of the Achaemenid Empire, built on an immense half-artificial, half-natural terrace with monumental relief stairways.
Strategically located on the Bosphorus peninsula between the Balkans and Anatolia, Istanbul has been associated with major political, religious and artistic events for over 2,000 years.
Universal symbols of the classical spirit and civilization, the sanctuaries erected on the rocky hill of Athens in the 5th century BC form the greatest architectural complex of Greek antiquity.

unesco_raw.name_en: Memphis and its Necropolis – the Pyramid Fields from Giza to Dahshur
unesco_raw.short_description_en: The capital of the Old Kingdom of Egypt has some extraordinary funerary monuments, including rock tombs, ornate mastabas, temples and pyramids, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
Standing 2,430 m above sea-level in a tropical mountain forest, Machu Picchu was probably the most amazing urban creation of the Inca Empire at its height.
Founded in the 9th century and home to the oldest university in the world, Fez reached its height in the 13th–14th centuries under the Marinids with its madrasas, fondouks, palaces and mosques.

unesco_raw.name_en: Monastery of the Hieronymites and Tower of Belém in Lisbon
unesco_raw.short_description_en: Standing at the entrance to Lisbon harbour, the Jerónimos Monastery and Tower of Belém exemplify Portuguese Manueline art at the height of the Age of Discoveries.

unesco_raw.name_en: Historic Centre of Salvador de Bahia
unesco_raw.short_description_en: As the first capital of Brazil from 1549 to 1763, Salvador witnessed the blending of European, African and Amerindian cultures and preserves bright colonial stucco buildings.
Made in Paris by the French sculptor Bartholdi in collaboration with Gustave Eiffel, this towering monument to liberty has welcomed millions at the entrance to New York Harbor since 1886.
The 13th-century merchants' town has Europe's largest market square and numerous historical houses, palaces and churches, along with the royal Wawel Castle.
Built between the 11th and 18th centuries, the Old Town, Lesser Town and New Town speak to the great architectural and cultural influence enjoyed by Prague since the Middle Ages.
The residence of the Habsburg monarchs from the 18th century to 1918, designed by Johann Bernhard Fischer von Erlach and Nicolaus Pacassi in a remarkably complete Baroque ensemble.
Founded in the 12th century on a hill surrounded by the Aare River, Bern has retained its medieval arcades, 16th-century fountains and historic sandstone streetscape.
An outstanding example of a medieval historic settlement, which has maintained its historic fabric over the centuries and was the cradle of the Flemish Primitives.

unesco_raw.name_en: Seventeenth-Century Canal Ring Area of Amsterdam inside the Singelgracht
unesco_raw.short_description_en: Designed at the end of the 16th century and built in the 17th century as a masterpiece of hydraulic engineering, town planning and bourgeois gabled architecture.

unesco_raw.name_en: Brú na Bóinne - Archaeological Ensemble of the Bend of the Boyne
unesco_raw.short_description_en: Europe's largest and most important concentration of prehistoric megalithic art, featuring the great passage tombs of Knowth, Newgrange and Dowth.
Inhabited since prehistoric times, this Nabataean caravan-city, situated between the Red Sea and the Dead Sea, is half-built, half-carved into the rose-red sandstone rock.
Stretching over some 400 sq. km, including forested area, Angkor Archaeological Park contains the magnificent remains of the different capitals of the Khmer Empire from the 9th to the 15th century.
An exceptionally well-preserved example of a South-East Asian trading port dating from the 15th to the 19th century, reflecting indigenous and foreign influences.
Famous Buddhist temple dating from the 8th and 9th centuries in central Java, built in three tiers: a pyramidal base, a trunk of cone with three circular platforms and a monumental stupa.
Eleven medieval monolithic cave churches carved directly into the volcanic rock in a 13th-century 'New Jerusalem' high in the mountains of Lasta.
The first colonial capital of Fiji, peacefully ceded to the British in 1874, developed from the early 19th century as a centre of commercial activity in the South Pacific.
Where the Althing, the open-air assembly representing the whole of Iceland, was established in 930 and continued to meet until 1798 across a dramatic volcanic rift valley.
